defects.description: A NaN price or dvol makes touch_fair return f = 1.0 instead of err. The `not S` / `r.get('dvol')` checks let NaN through (NaN is truthy). The closed form then evaluates to NaN, and `min(1.0, nan)` in one_touch returns 1.0, a confident wrong fair. A NaN running high/low reads as untouched. I verified this with verify.py: NaN price gives 1.0, NaN dvol gives 1.0. Nothing is wired and the inputs come from JSON feeds, so this is low risk, but it goes against the 'never guesses' intent.
defects.fix_hint: In touch_fair, return {'err': ...} unless math.isfinite holds for S, H, sq and ext. Alternatively, in one_touch, return the raw value or guard the NaN before the min(1.0, ...) clamp so it does not turn into 1.0.

defects.description: coherence_flags (via eps -> call_over_h) raises ZeroDivisionError when tau_h <= 0 or sigma == 0 on an up-touch with both books two-sided. bounds() has the same problem through ladder.digital. A log-only scan run at or after the window end would crash instead of returning [].
defects.fix_hint: In coherence_flags, skip the upper check (or return []) when tau_h <= 0 or sigma <= 0. Or note in the wiring notes that callers must pass tau_h > 0.
